Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the run-chase! The Irish players are out there in the middle. Innocent Kaia and Wesley Madhevere are the openers for Zimbabwe. Mark Adair to start with the ball. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, Ireland have posted a good total of 288 on the board and they will be hoping for their bowlers to defend it. For Zimbabwe, the onus is now on their batters to put up a gritty stand and win it in front of their home crowd. Which side will get over the line? Let's find out together. Chase coming up shortly...

The Zimbabwean pacers started off well and got the assistance of the pitch. They managed to get both the Irish openers early on but lost their way after that. They tried hard to break the Balbirnie-Tector partnership but just couldn't do it. They will be upset with how things went after the Powerplay. They did manage to get some wickets at the end, but the damage was already done. Victor Nyauchi took two wickets whilst Sikandar Raza and Richard Ngarava has one in their kitty.

A wonderful display of batting from the visitors after having a bad start from the openers. They lost both of their openers inside powerplay and were reeling at 25/2 inside 9 overs. Andy Balbirnie and Harry Tector joined hands after that and ran a havoc over the Zimbabwe bowlers. Andy Balbirnie got chances couple of times at the start but he went on to score his 8th ODI century. They stitched a record breaking partnership of 212 runs for the third wicket. Andy Balbirnie was retired hurt after that on a nasty full toss from Evans. They lost a couple of quick wickets at the back end but Harry Tector carried on with his flurry of runs and went on to score his 3rd ODI century.
On a length and on off, Lorcan Tucker lofts it towards long on. The ball goes up in the air and lands safely. They collect two. Ireland end their innings at 288/4 after their 50 overs.

Hundred up for Harry Tector! Fuller one on off, Harry Tector squeezes it to covers and scampers for a couple of runs to bring up his century! What a knock this has been from the young man, he continues to go from strength to strength. He is absolutely delighted and soaks in the applause from this teammates and the crowd here at the Harare Sports Club.

Commentary.Howout: c Ryan Burl b Victor Nyauchi

OUT! CAUGHT! George Dockrell holes out in the deep and this dangerous looking small partnership is broken. Raza is the man who provides the breakthrough! A full toss, around waist height, around off. Dockrell tries to loft it over the fence towards the off side. However, he fails to get enough power behind this shot and ends up hitting it straight to Ryan Burl at deep cover. He takes the catch comfortably and Raza has the last laugh.

Drinks! Ireland have recovered very well after losing Stephen Doheny and Paul Stirling early on in the first Powerplay. Both Andy Balbirnie and Tector have survived some close chances and are now are looking all set to launch from here. Zimbabwe need to find breakthrough or this game can run away from them very quickly. Their spinners have not been able to put much pressure on the Irish batters and it would be interesting to see how the action unfolds in the final 15 overs. Sikandar Raza is back on.

Victor Nyauchi and Richard Ngarava have one wicket each but Victor Nyauchi got close to get another one number of times and Zimbabwe would be hoping to continue in the same vain. Irish batters have been cautious in testing conditions and this partnership between Andy Balbirnie and Harry Tector is key for them now.

On a good length, on off. Andy Balbirnie blocks it off the back foot nicely.
Back of a length and outside off. Tector pushes it past point for a single.

Oh, just short of Raza at first slip! Lands it on a good length, around off. Gets a good shape away from the batter and Tector who tries to defend it from his crease, gets an outside edge. The ball goes left of Raza at first slip and falls just short of him as he puts in a dive.
WIDE! On a length and it is down the leg side. Tector tries to flick it but misses.
Goes fuller and on leg. Andy Balbirnie flicks it to fine leg for a single.
Serves it on a good length again and outside off. Tector makes another leave.
On a length, and outside off. Tector leaves it alone.
Harry Tector is the new man.

OUT! LBW! Richard Ngarava strikes and Paul Stirling departs! This is a huge, huge wicket for Zimbabwe! Richard Ngarava goes fuller after keeping it a bit short in the previous deliveries. It is on middle and it swings away from Paul Stirling at the last moment. Paul Stirling tries to flick it but misses and gets hit on the pads. Richard Ngarava makes a loud appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Paul Stirling though is not happy and looks very disappointed. No DRS for this series and he has to walk back.
Back of a length, on off. It is angled across but Paul Stirling covers the line of the ball and defends it.
Lands it on a length, around off. Paul Stirling goes back and defends it without much fuss.
Back of a length, on off. Paul Stirling punches it nicely to covers.
WIDE! Goes fuller and it swings down the leg side. Paul tries to flick it but misses.
Maiden to start from Evans! On a length, on off. Tad shorter maybe and Andy Balbirnie transfers his weight on the back foot to defend it again.
Good bowling. Continues to bowl in that channel, outside off as Andy Balbirnie is just happy to defend it out.
Serves it on a length and shaping away. Andy is solid in his defence again.
Goes fuller and on middle. Andy Balbirnie drives it to the mid off fielder.
Hits that good length again, around off. Andy Balbirnie dabs it towards the cover-point fielder.
Starts off with a good-length delivery. It is around off and Andy Balbirnie fends it from his crease.
Brad Evans comes into the attack now.
Touch short of full length, on middle. It nips back in a bit. Paul Stirling tries to work it towards the leg side but misses. The ball hits him high on the pads.
Lands it on a length, on off. Paul Stirling fends it calmly.
A fullish delivery on middle. Paul Stirling clips it to the square leg fielder. Good bowling.
On a length and outside off. Andy Balbirnie steers it towards third man for a single.
Nice delivery! Lands it on a length and around off. The ball goes across the right-hander and Andy Balbirnie gets beaten as he tries to defend it.
Back of a length, on middle. Andy Balbirnie defends it towards the short mid-wicket fielder.

FOUR! Width provided and Paul Stirling gets another boundary! This is full and outside off. Paul Stirling drives it off the outside half of his blade. The ball goes over the point fielder and runs away towards the fence.
Back of a length and on off. Paul Stirling with a solid block off the back foot.
Back of a length and angling into middle. Paul Stirling tries to clip it but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Serves a fullish delivery on middle. Paul Stirling defends it towards the leg side.
Goes fuller and on leg. Andy Balbirnie flicks it to fine leg for a single.
Lands it on a length, on middle. Paul Stirling works it to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length, on leg. Paul Stirling clips it to fine leg for a single. This has been a cautious start from the Irish.
Overpitched and outside off. Paul Stirling drives it nicely again but straight to the cover fielder this time.
Lands it on a length and outside off. The ball seams away and Paul Stirling leaves it alone nicely.
FOUR! Finds the gap! This is full and outside off. Paul Stirling takes a big stride forward and drives it bit uppishly but in the gap through covers for a boundary.
Goes fuller and swinging into middle. Andy Balbirnie pushes it off the inside half of his blade towards the leg side for a single.
Back of a length, on middle. Andy Balbirnie tries to clip it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Lands it on a length, on off. Paul Stirling blocks it right under his eyes. Another good over from Victor Nyauchi!
On a length and around off. Andy Balbirnie steers it towards third man for a single.
Back of a length, on off. Andy Balbirnie fends it off the back foot.
Angles a length delivery on middle. Paul Stirling works it past square leg for a single.
Lands it on a length, on off. Paul Stirling defends it this time.
Victor is getting nice movement here! A fullish delivery and outside off. The ball shapes away and Paul Stirling goes for an expensive drive, only to get beaten.
Goes fuller this time to find some swing. Bowls it on middle and Andy Balbirnie blocks it towards the leg side.
Back of a length, on off. Andy Balbirnie stays back and defends it nicely.
Back of a length, on middle. Paul Stirling works it to square leg and takes a single.
Serves it on a length again, on off. Paul Stirling dabs it towards the off side again.
Lands it on a length, on off. Paul Stirling fends it off the front foot.

A stifled appeal from the bowler but maybe pitching outside leg. Lands this around leg and it goes across Paul Stirling as he tries to defend it. The ball hits him on the back leg but it is little high too and the umpire denies the appeal.
Lands it on a length, on off. Andy Balbirnie fends it solidly off the front foot.
FOUR! Confident start from Andy Balbirnie! Overpitched and outside off. Andy Balbirnie leans forward and caresses it through covers for a lovely boundary.
The skipper, Andy Balbirnie walks in.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Here it is... Victor Nyauchi with a big-inswinger and draws first blood! This is full and swinging into Stephen Doheny from off. He tries to drive it with a big stride forward. However, the ball manages to find the gap between bat and pad and knocks over the stumps. Zimbabwe get an early breakthrough!
On a length, on off. Stephen Doheny fends it right under his eyes.
An overpitched delivery and outside off. Stephen Doheny drives it to the cover fielder.
Bowls a fullish delivery on middle. It swings into Stephen Doheny and he gets hit on the pads as he misses his drive. A half-appeal follows but it is going down leg.
Victor Nyauchi will bowl from the other end.

Oh, direct hit and Paul Stirling was a goner! On a length, on middle. Stephen Doheny works it right of square leg and the batters go for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the batter's end but misses and Ireland get another run on the board.
Serves it on a good length, shaping into middle. Doheny is happy to block it again.
On a length again, on off. Stephen Doheny with a solid block off the front foot again.
Lands on a length, on off. Stephen Doheny fends it towards the off side.
A fullish delivery on middle. Doheny works it right of mid on and takes couple of runs. He is off the mark as well.
Starts off with a back-of-a-length delivery on leg. Paul Stirling clips it to square leg for a single. Ireland and Stirling are underway!

We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires have made their way out in the middle. Zimbabwe players are seen in a huddle, near the ropes. Paul Stirling and Stephen Doheny are the openers for Ireland. Richard Ngarava to start with the new ball. Here we go...

Pitch Report - Darlington says that the wicket looks brown and hard and there is moisture underneath in the pitch. Tells that the captain who win the toss would be looking to chase and says that 210-220 would be a competitive score on this pitch and feels that batting will be difficult early on.

Andy Balbirnie, the skipper of Ireland says that wanted to bowl as well. Adds that they have given opportunities to some new players as they missed some games. Says that they struggled in the T20 but they will be stronger now. Ends by saying that they have good players and they will look to win this one.

Craig Ervine, the skipper of Zimbabwe says that they will bowl first. Adds that the pitch has been in cover for the last day and a half and feels that there will be help for the seamers and they would like to exploit that. Tells that he expects the pitch to get better to bat but hopes to take some early wickets. Informs that Raza is back and Ballance is also fit and informs that Chatara is resting today.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Stephen Doheny, Andy Balbirnie (C), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Andy McBrine, Mark Adair, Graham Hume, Josh Little.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Innocent Kaia, Wesley Madhevere, Craig Ervine (C), Gary Ballance, Sikandar Raza, Ryan Burl, Clive Madande (WK), Wellington Masakadza, Brad Evans, Richard Ngarava, Victor Nyauchi.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and will BOWL first.

Ireland, on the other hand, are a strong ODI unit too. They have almost all bases covered with quality and experienced batters along with all-rounders and pacers. However, inconsistency has been an issue in Irish cricket for a long time now and they would like to rectify that in a year where ODI cricket takes a prime position. Can they start off the series with a win? Or will Zimbabwe continue their path to a renaissance? Let’s find out. Toss and team news in a while.

Zimbabwe have played some quality cricket in the recent past and it is time for them to reaffirm that and make a strong statement by beating Ireland in an ODI series ahead of the World Cup Qualifier. They have Sikandar Raza back in the mix after the star-allrounder missed the T20I series and with Gary Ballance also joining Zimbabwean cricket, things are only going to get better for Zimbabwe. Let’s see how the home team goes about its business.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks! It is time for the first ODI of this three-match ODI series between Zimbabwe and Ireland. We witnessed an entertaining T20I series with Zimbabwean crowd getting right behind their boys and turning up in huge numbers. So, expect the ODI series to follow the same suit and dish out another thrilling series between these two evenly-matched teams. Our not-so-beloved friend, may play the spoilsport though and let’s hope that rain stays away and we see cricket taking the centrestage here at the Harare Sports Club.
... MATCH DAY …

We are all ready for the ODI series between Zimbabwe and Ireland and we can expect some quality and thrilling cricket after what we saw in a recently concluded T20I series. The games were intense and pretty closely fought and the ODI series promises to go in the same vain. This is the 50-over World Cup year and this series will provide ideal preparation for both sides as they might face off each other in the Qualifier in Zimbabwe later this year if Ireland fails to seal the eighth spot in the World Cup Super League. So, we have some big guns from both teams coming back after missing the T20I series. For Ireland, the likes of Paul Stirling, Joshua Little are back to name a few while for Zimbabwe, their most prolific performer in 2022, Sikandar Raza is back in the mix. Zimbabwe were brilliant in 2022 with a series win over Bangladesh and an ODI win against Australia in the land of Kangaroos. Ireland too have been playing some good ODI cricket and though they lost to Kiwis, the series was pretty competitive and Ireland surely have the resources to get results on their side in this series. The Irish batting unit looks pretty solid with the experience of Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie to go with some talented batters like Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker and George Dockrell. Curtis Campher and Andy McBrine provide them balance with their all-round skills and with Josh Little also back for national duty, Ireland look like a well-oiled unit. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, will miss the services of  Sean Williams due to an injury he suffered in the T20I series but they have their captain, Craig Ervine, back in form now. Sikandar Raza though would be a key player once again and if he continues to show the form he showed in 2022, then we surely will see some happy faces in a passionate crowd that is expected to cheer their home team at the  Harare Sports Club. The presence of experienced player like Gary Ballance also would add as a huge boost and let's see how he goes about his business in his new venture. Ryan Burl is another player who will need to take centrestage just like he did in the T20I series and if youngsters in the Zimbabwean team can come up with more significant performances, they can have another crack at a series win here. The first game of a three-match ODI series is always very important and it would be interesting to see which team comes up on top in the opening ODI of this series. Can Zimbabwe carry the momentum of the T20I series and go 1-0 up? Or will Irish boys excel in the longer format? Let’s find out.
